newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids again steadied by firmer crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids again steadied by firmer crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices again stayed little changed Monday in thin trade, still underpinned by a firmer crude market despite the lack of East Coast utility demand, market sources said.

"The fundamentals are rather weak, but prices are already at low levels. Demand may not be there, but I think we're at or near bottom in resid," said one cash trader, noting East Coast forecasts this week offered little hope for better loads.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent held relatively steady at about $16.00 a barrel, with July one percent paper talked down slightly at $15.55-75 despite gains in crude.
Traders said early NYH paper quotes for August were in the $15.70 area, with September at $15.30-55 and Q3 at $15.45-70.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally was unchanged at $16.75.
High sulphurs in New York also held steady, with 2.2 percent still pegged in the $14.50-75 area, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again were stable, with three percent still talked on either side of $14.50 and one percent at about $16.00.

New York city gate gas prices climbed by about five cents to the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.31 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained a similar amount to $2.19/mmBtu, or $13.80 a barrel.
